DeepSeek's 100 billion yuan funding round closes: 31 investors assemble, with Tencent and CATL tied as largest backers
Add preferred source
DeepSeek's second funding round, sized at 100 billion yuan, has completed its business registration change. The registered capital of operating entity Hangzhou DeepSeek rose to 19.918707 million yuan (approximately $3.0 million), an increase of about 21.1%. Holding platform Hangzhou Chengyan added 31 partners, with committed capital jumping from 6,000 yuan (approximately $900) to 3.438979 billion yuan (approximately $515.9 million). Tencent and CATL each hold 9.5653%, tied as the largest contributors; China Mobile and CITIC Securities each hold 7.6522%, and Monolith Capital holds 7.1740%. China Telecom, vivo, Midea and Meituan Longzhu are also on the list. Existing shareholders received priority allocations, and DeepSeek set requirements on industrial synergy while retaining strong control over deal terms. Market sources say DeepSeek has hired CITIC Securities to prepare a STAR Market IPO and plans to launch the listing process this year.
Key Elements
DeepSeek Hangzhou DeepSeek Artificial Intelligence Basic Technology Research Co. Ltd. Hangzhou Chengyan Enterprise Management Consulting Partnership Tencent CATL China Mobile CITIC Securities Monolith Capital Liang Wenfeng Xiaohongshu NetEase vivo GigaDevice STAR Market
The closely watched second funding round of DeepSeek, sized at 100 billion yuan, has officially closed. Business registration records show that its operating entity, Hangzhou DeepSeek Artificial Intelligence Basic Technology Research Co., Ltd., recently completed a registration change, adding new shareholder Hangzhou Chengyan Enterprise Management Consulting Partnership (limited partnership). Registered capital rose to 19.918707 million yuan (approximately $3.0 million), an increase of about 21.1%.
Looking up the ownership chain, Hangzhou Chengyan also completed a registration change over the same period, adding 31 partners and lifting its registered committed capital from 6,000 yuan (approximately $900) to 3.438979 billion yuan (approximately $515.9 million). After the change, the holding platform has 32 partners, with Hangzhou Chengce Business Consulting Co., Ltd. continuing as executive partner. The 31 new partners are the external shareholders that participated in this round of DeepSeek financing, spanning industrial players including Tencent, China Mobile, China Telecom, CATL, GigaDevice, Xiaohongshu and vivo, as well as investment institutions such as Monolith, Boyu, IDG, Gaorong, Legend Capital, Firstred Capital and CITIC Securities.
By contribution structure, Tencent's Shanghai Hengxiu Business Management Co., Ltd. ranks first with a 9.5653% share. CATL invested through three funds — Xiamen Shidai Yiyuan, Xiamen Shidai Shenyuan and Fujian Shidai Zeyuan — at 4.9198%, 4.4410% and 0.2045% respectively, for a combined 9.5653%, tying Tencent as the largest contributor. China Mobile's China Mobile Investment Holdings Co., Ltd. and CITIC Securities Investment Co., Ltd. each hold 7.6522%; Monolith Capital's related Tianjin Monolith Xingshen Equity Investment Partnership (limited partnership) holds 7.1740%.

Toyota is looking beyond the automotive industry as it places bigger bets on robotics, physical AI, energy, aerospace, and other emerging technologies. Through its venture arm, Woven Capital , the automaker is investing in startups that could help shape what the company looks like decades from now. But as startup valuations climb and competition for promising companies intensifies, figuring out where the next big opportunities lie is becoming increasingly important.
On this episode of TechCrunch’s ⁠Equity⁠ podcast, transportation editor Kirsten Korosec is joined by ⁠Ro Gupta⁠ , head of ⁠Woven Capital⁠ and former founder of autonomous vehicle startup Carmera, to discuss Toyota’s investment strategy, the changing venture capital landscape, and what’s next for emerging technology. Listen to the full episode to hear about:
Why Ro thinks today’s sky-high startup valuations may be more justified than they first appear, and whether there are enough worthwhile companies to warrant the investment.
How the autonomous vehicle boom of 2017 and 2018 compares to today’s AI frenzy, and why future technology hype cycles could move faster.
Why Toyota is investing beyond its traditional automotive business, from robotics and physical AI to energy, aerospace, and manufacturing.
What Woven Capital looks for in startups, why manufacturing and supply chain technology are suddenly attracting attention, and how Toyota’s industrial expertise can give portfolio companies an advantage.
Why corporate venture capital has become more attractive to founders, and how strategic investors can offer more than just money through customers, manufacturing capabilities, and global distribution.
Where the next opportunities in autonomous vehicles are emerging, and why the biggest investments may now be in the infrastructure and operations that make autonomous fleets work at scale.

She is also co-founder and co-host of the podcast, “The Autonocast.” She previously wrote for Fortune, The Verge, Bloomberg, MIT Technology Review and CBS Interactive.
